metadata.title: Top US Finance News
metadata.ranking_basis: Ranked by market impact and breadth of coverage on Friday, October 9, 2026. Rank 1 is the index close. The rest follow in order of the size of the market move and how widely established outlets covered them: the telecom rout, the consumer sentiment data, the Russia diesel announcement and oil, the Fed governor inquiry, then single-company stories and the bond and gold close.
metadata.fact_check_method: Researched by web search, then every story was re-checked against its sources in a second pass; facts and stories the re-check could not support were removed.

verification_status_legend.verified: Key facts confirmed by a primary source or by two or more independent sources
verification_status_legend.partially_verified: Core event confirmed, but one or more specific figures rest on a single source or sources conflict

limitations: Compiled by the pipeline's news step by web search.

Several pages could not be opened (AP via Washington Post and WUSA9, CNBC, Axios, Quartz, The Hill, Globe and Mail, ETF Trends, TheStreet). For those stories I relied on other pages I could open plus search-result summaries of the blocked ones; the affected stories are marked partially_verified.

Index closes use the AP figures (opened on two AP syndication pages and matching the Yahoo Finance live blog). One search summary and Investrade showed slightly different values (Dow 51,655.01, +423.37 or +423.54; S&P 500 7,811.51, +46.15 or +46.16); these were not used.
Moderna's move is reported as 14% in a Yahoo Finance article and 9% in the Yahoo Finance live blog; the closing move was not confirmed, so no exact percent is given as a key fact.
The 10-year Treasury yield close is reported as 5.24% (Yahoo Finance, ETF Trends) and 5.27% (Investrade); the official Treasury or Fed H.15 figure for October 9 was not available to check.
Closing share prices for Apple and Delta were not confirmed; only early-trading moves are given.
The Federal Reserve's calendar showed no Fed speeches or releases on October 9, so there is no monetary-policy story from the Fed itself.
The consensus forecast for consumer sentiment differed between sources (47.3 and 47.8) and for Delta's EPS (1.82 and 1.89); neither consensus is given as a key fact.
'Gold rose about 1.4% to roughly $4,216 an ounce as the 10-year Treasury yield eased for a second day to about 5.24%.': removed 1 key fact(s) the re-check could not support.

stories.headline: The Dow rose 423.31 points to 51,654.95 and the S&P 500 gained 0.6% to 7,811.54 as Wall Street closed out a record-setting week.
stories.summary: US stocks rose on Friday to end a record-setting week. The S&P 500 climbed 0.6% and came close to the all-time high it set three days earlier. The S&P 500, Dow and Nasdaq all posted weekly gains, while the small-company Russell 2000 fell for the week.
key_facts: The S&P 500 rose 46.18 points, or 0.6%, to 7,811.54.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 423.31 points, or 0.8%, to 51,654.95.
The Nasdaq composite rose 172.83 points, or 0.6%, to 27,366.17.
The Russell 2000 rose 12.85 points, or 0.5%, to 2,806.98.
For the week, the S&P 500 gained 88.82 points, or 1.2%.
For the week, the Dow gained 477.99 points, or 0.9%.
For the week, the Nasdaq gained 175.31 points, or 0.6%.
For the week, the Russell 2000 fell 25.91 points, or 0.9%.
For the year, the S&P 500 is up 14.1%, the Dow is up 7.5% and the Nasdaq is up 17.7%.
The S&P 500 came close to topping its all-time high set three days earlier.

fact_check.notes: Closing levels, point moves, weekly and year-to-date figures come from the AP 'How major US stock indexes fared' report, opened on two syndication pages (Mankato Free Press, KRMG), and match the Yahoo Finance live blog. Investrade and one search summary show slightly different Dow and S&P figures (Dow 51,655.01; S&P 7,811.51); AP figures are used.

stories.headline: T-Mobile fell 13.27%, AT&T 9.81% and Verizon 8.75% after SpaceX agreed to buy 800 MHz spectrum for Starlink Mobile.
stories.summary: Shares of the three big US wireless carriers sank on Friday after SpaceX announced on Thursday an agreement to buy a nationwide spectrum portfolio from Grain Management. SpaceX said the low-band spectrum would pave the way for Starlink Mobile to become a major US mobile carrier. The deal needs approval from the Federal Communications Commission.
key_facts: T-Mobile shares dropped 13.27%, their worst day since 2013.
AT&T shares fell 9.81%, their worst day since 2000.
Verizon shares closed down 8.75%, their worst day since July 2002.
SpaceX agreed to acquire up to 14 megahertz of paired spectrum in the 800 MHz band from Grain Management.
The deal is valued at roughly $8 billion, according to the Wall Street Journal.
The deal is subject to approval by the Federal Communications Commission.
SpaceX shares rose about 1% on the day.

fact_check.notes: The three closing percentage moves match between the Yahoo Finance live blog (opened) and CNBC's report (seen in search summary; page blocked). Deal terms are confirmed in the Yahoo Finance/Quartz article (opened). The $8 billion value is a Wall Street Journal report, not a company figure. SpaceX's gain is given as about 1% by CNBC and 1.6% by the Yahoo live blog. The deal was announced Thursday, October 8; the full-session share drop happened on October 9.

stories.headline: US consumer sentiment fell to 46.3 in early October, a five-month low, as year-ahead inflation expectations rose to 4.7%.
stories.summary: The University of Michigan's preliminary consumer sentiment index dropped to 46.3 in October from 48.1 in September, the lowest reading since May. Survey director Joanne Hsu said frustration over the cost of living continues to mount. Inflation expectations edged up for both the year ahead and the long run.
key_facts: The University of Michigan preliminary consumer sentiment index fell to 46.3 in October from 48.1 in September.
The reading is the lowest since May, a five-month low.
The current economic conditions index fell to 44.7.
The consumer expectations index rose to 47.3.
Year-ahead inflation expectations rose to 4.7% from 4.6%.
Five-year inflation expectations rose to 3.5% from 3.4%.
Survey director Joanne Hsu said: "Frustration over cost-of-living continues to mount."
entities: University of Michigan Surveys of Consumers

fact_check.notes: Headline index, prior reading and inflation expectations are confirmed by Yahoo Finance (opened), Investrade (opened) and search summaries of Bloomberg, Reuters via US News and Advisor Perspectives. The sub-indexes (44.7 and 47.3) match between Investrade and Advisor Perspectives. Consensus forecasts differed between sources (47.3 and 47.8) and are not included. The University of Michigan's own release was not opened.

stories.headline: Trump said Russia will immediately supply over 300,000 tons of diesel, while Brent crude settled up 44 cents at $104.72 a barrel.
stories.summary: President Donald Trump said on Friday that Russia had agreed to immediately supply more than 300,000 tons of diesel to the US and global market after a discussion with Vladimir Putin he called "highly successful". He said further supplies would follow in November and after. Oil dipped on the announcement but settled higher as a hurricane shut Gulf of Mexico production.
key_facts: Trump said Russia agreed to immediately supply over 300,000 tons of diesel fuel to the American and global marketplace.
Trump said Russia would supply another 500,000 tons in November and 1 million tons immediately thereafter.
Trump described his discussion with Vladimir Putin as "highly successful".
Brent crude futures settled at $104.72 a barrel, up 44 cents, or 0.42%.
US West Texas Intermediate crude settled at $91.85 a barrel, up 36 cents, or 0.39%.
Oil companies shut more than 70% of crude production in US Gulf of Mexico waters ahead of Hurricane Isaias.

fact_check.notes: The diesel announcement and tonnage are confirmed by Al Jazeera (opened), the Yahoo Finance live blog (opened) and search summaries of Reuters via the Globe and Mail and MarketScreener. Oil settlement prices match between Investrade (opened) and a Reuters settlement report (search summary). Not included as key facts because each rests on one source: a Treasury general license allowing Russian diesel imports until April 7 next year (Reuters via Globe and Mail, search summary only) and a US diesel price of $6.27 a gallon (Al Jazeera). Trump also referred to 3 million tons in total; sources word that figure differently, so it is omitted.

stories.headline: Trump created a three-person committee to investigate mortgage fraud allegations against Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook.
stories.summary: President Donald Trump on Friday formally established a "committee of inquiry" to investigate allegations that Fed Governor Lisa Cook made false statements on mortgage documents. The panel is made up of three executive branch officials, including Trump economic adviser Kevin Hassett. Cook has strongly contested the allegations.
key_facts: Trump announced a three-person committee to investigate mortgage fraud allegations against Fed Governor Lisa Cook.
The panel is called a "committee of inquiry".
The committee is made up of three executive branch officials, including Kevin Hassett.
The committee is to hold an in-person hearing at the White House on November 5.
Lisa Cook has served on the Federal Reserve Board since 2022 and has contested the allegations.

fact_check.notes: The committee's creation on October 9 is reported by Bloomberg, CNBC, CNN, The Hill and SCOTUSblog and is noted in the Yahoo Finance live blog (opened). The other pages could not be opened, so the details come from search-result summaries. The November 5 hearing date and Hassett's membership appeared in those summaries and were not checked against a page I opened.

stories.headline: Delta Air Lines reported adjusted earnings of $1.72 a share and a full-year outlook of $5.10 to $5.60 as fuel expense jumped 62%.
stories.summary: Delta Air Lines reported September-quarter results on Friday, with adjusted revenue of $17.6 billion, up 16% from a year earlier. Adjusted fuel expense rose 62% to $4.1 billion, and adjusted earnings per share of $1.72 missed analyst estimates. The airline's full-year earnings outlook of $5.10 to $5.60 a share is down from a previous $6.50 to $7.50.
key_facts: Delta reported September-quarter adjusted earnings per share of $1.72, versus $1.70 a year earlier.
Delta's GAAP earnings per share were $1.15, down from $2.17.
Adjusted operating revenue was $17.6 billion, up 16% from a year earlier.
Adjusted fuel expense was $4.1 billion, up 62% from a year earlier.
Delta's adjusted fuel price was $3.61 a gallon, up 60% from a year earlier.
Delta's full-year earnings outlook is $5.10 to $5.60 a share, down from a previous $6.50 to $7.50.
Delta expects December-quarter revenue to grow approximately 20%.
Delta expects full-year free cash flow of approximately $2.5 billion.
Delta shares fell about 4% to around $79 in early trading.

fact_check.notes: Results and outlook come from Delta's press release filed with the SEC on Form 8-K (opened). The prior guidance of $6.50 to $7.50 is from TipRanks and Investrade, not the release. The analyst EPS estimate differs by source ($1.82 in Yahoo Finance and TipRanks, $1.89 in Investrade), so it is not a key fact. The early-trading share drop is from TipRanks; the closing move was not confirmed, and the Yahoo live blog suggests the stock recovered by the close.

stories.headline: Moderna shares jumped to their highest level since January 2022 after a report on a national cancer vaccine effort starting in December.
stories.summary: Moderna stock surged on Friday after the New York Times reported new details of an effort led by the National Institutes of Health to speed up cancer vaccine development. The public-private partnership is expected to start in December. Other vaccine makers, including Novavax, Pfizer, BioNTech and Merck, also rose.
key_facts: Moderna stock hit its highest level since January 2022.
Moderna is up more than 600% so far in 2026, the best-performing stock in the S&P 500 this year.
The New York Times reported new details of a National Institutes of Health effort to accelerate cancer vaccine development.
The cancer vaccine program is expected to start in December.
The program is expected to focus on pancreatic, liver and colorectal cancer and certain pediatric tumors.
Novavax, Pfizer, BioNTech and Merck shares also gained.

fact_check.notes: The rally and its cause are confirmed by a Yahoo Finance article (opened), the Yahoo Finance live blog (opened) and Investrade (opened). The size of the move is not settled: the Yahoo article says 14%, the Yahoo live blog says 9%. The year-to-date gain is given as 662% in one and 627% in the other. No exact percent is given as a key fact; 'more than 600%' is consistent with both. Novavax's 15% gain rests on the Yahoo article alone and is omitted.

stories.headline: Apple shares fell more than 2.5% in early trading after a report that it cut iPhone 18 Pro component orders by at least 15%.
stories.summary: Apple shares dropped early on Friday after Nikkei Asia reported the company is cutting iPhone 18 Pro component orders because of weaker-than-expected demand. October orders were reportedly reduced by at least 15%. Higher memory costs and $100 price increases were cited as weighing on demand, and the stock partly recovered later in the day.
key_facts: Apple shares fell more than 2.5% in early trading.
Nikkei Asia reported Apple cut October component orders for the iPhone 18 Pro by at least 15%.
The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max each cost $100 more than their predecessors.
The iPhone 18 Pro starts at $1,199 and the Pro Max at $1,299.
The report cited weaker-than-expected demand and high memory costs.

fact_check.notes: The order cut is a Nikkei Asia report, not an Apple statement; Apple has not confirmed it. The report and the early share drop are confirmed by MacRumors (opened), Investrade (opened) and search summaries of Forbes, Benzinga and Investing.com. The starting prices come from a search summary only. Apple's closing move was not confirmed; sources say the stock partly recovered.

stories.headline: Aircraft lessor Avolon ordered 250 jets, including 140 Boeing 737 MAX and 110 Airbus aircraft.
stories.summary: Avolon announced on Friday firm orders for 250 aircraft from Boeing and Airbus. The order covers 140 Boeing 737 MAX jets, 75 Airbus A320neo family aircraft and 35 A330neo family aircraft, plus options for 100 more Airbus planes. It is conditional on approval by majority shareholder Bohai Leasing, expected before October 31.
key_facts: Avolon ordered 250 aircraft from Airbus and Boeing.
The order includes 140 Boeing 737 MAX jets.
The order includes 75 Airbus A320neo family aircraft and 35 Airbus A330neo family aircraft.
Avolon also took options on 100 additional Airbus aircraft.
The orders raise Avolon's total firm aircraft commitments to 749.
The orders are conditional on approval by Bohai Leasing, Avolon's 70% shareholder, expected before October 31, 2026.

fact_check.notes: Figures come from Avolon's Business Wire press release dated October 9, 2026 (opened via FinancialContent) and match Investrade and trade-press coverage (FlightGlobal, AviTrader, Aviation Week in search results). No share-price reaction for Boeing or Airbus was confirmed.

stories.headline: Gold rose about 1.4% to roughly $4,216 an ounce as the 10-year Treasury yield eased for a second day to about 5.24%.
stories.summary: Gold firmed on Friday as a softer dollar and easing Treasury yields boosted its appeal, recovering from a two-month low hit on Wednesday. The 10-year Treasury yield slipped for a second straight session after touching its highest level since 2002 earlier in the week.
key_facts: December gold futures rose $59.30, or 1.43%, to $4,216.30 an ounce.
Gold hit a two-month low on Wednesday before rebounding.
The 2-year Treasury yield ended at 4.80%.
The 10-year Treasury yield touched its highest level since 2002 on Wednesday.

fact_check.notes: The gold futures settlement ($4,216.30, +$59.30, +1.43%) rests on Investrade alone; the Yahoo Finance live blog showed a later quote of 4,220.30, up 63.30 (1.52%). The 10-year yield is 5.24% in Yahoo Finance and ETF Trends (search summary) but 5.27% in Investrade; the official Treasury figure was not checked. The 2-year yield of 4.80% rests on ETF Trends alone. The direction of both moves and the weekly context are confirmed by CNBC and BabyPips search summaries. Re-check: Gold: Investrade (opened) confirms December gold settled +$59.30 (+1.43%) at $4,216.30; the two-month low on Wednesday October 7 is supported by Mining.com and Mitrade search results. The 10-year yield's highest level since 2002 (about 5.36%) on Wednesday October 7 is supported by Forbes, FXStreet and BigGo search results. The 2-year at 4.80% and 10-year at 5.24% rest on an ETF Trends search summary only (page returned 403). The 10-year close and the 'second straight session' decline are not firmly supported: Investrade gives 5.27%; Trading Economics shows 5.23% to 5.24%, described once as 'held steady' and once as down 0.01 point; CNBC had the yield at 5.229% during Thursday's session, which would make 5.24% on Friday flat to slightly higher. No opened source states a second consecutive daily decline, and the CNBC gold page was blocked. The headline repeats the 'eased for a second day to about 5.24%' claim.
